title: Luke Chapter 5 Quiz - Multi-Level
description: An enhanced quiz on Luke chapter 5 with Easy, Medium, Hard, and Theological levels. Each level has 15 carefully crafted questions. Choose your difficulty and dive in!

easy.title: Luke Chapter 5 Quiz - Easy Level
easy.description: Perfect for beginners! Test your basic knowledge of Luke Chapter 5.

questions.question: In Luke 5, which of the following appears FIRST in the chapter?
options: Jesus stood by the lake of Gennesaret
A man full of leprosy approached Jesus
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus stood by the lake of Gennesaret
questions.explanation: This event is the first mentioned in the chapter, as stated in Luke 5:1.

questions.question: What were the fishermen doing when Jesus saw them?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:2 states that the fishermen were gone out of their ships and were washing their nets.

questions.question: Whose ship did Jesus enter?
questions.explanation: According to Luke 5:3, Jesus entered into Simon's ship.

questions.question: What did Jesus ask Simon to do after he finished speaking?
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed Simon to launch out into the deep and let down his nets for a draught as per Luke 5:4.

questions.question: What did Simon say after Jesus told him to let down the net?
options: We have toiled all the night
We caught a lot of fish
questions.correctAnswer: We have toiled all the night
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:5, Simon answered that they had toiled all night and had taken nothing.

questions.question: What happened when Simon let down the net?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:6 states that they inclosed a great multitude of fishes, and their net broke.

questions.question: Who did Simon beckon to help him with the catch?
questions.explanation: As stated in Luke 5:7, Simon beckoned unto his partners who were in the other ship to help them.

questions.question: What did Simon Peter say when he saw the catch of fish?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:8 records that Simon Peter fell down at Jesus' knees, saying, 'Depart from me; for I am a sinful man, O Lord.'

questions.question: Who was astonished at the draught of fishes?
questions.explanation: According to Luke 5:9, all that were with Simon were astonished at the draught of the fishes.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell Simon he would catch from now on?
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:10, Jesus said unto Simon, 'Fear not; from henceforth thou shalt catch men.'

questions.question: What did Simon and the others do after bringing their ships to land?
options: They forsook all and followed him
questions.correctAnswer: They forsook all and followed him
questions.explanation: Luke 5:11 states that they forsook all and followed Jesus after bringing their ships to land.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus healed a man with leprosy in this chapter.
questions.explanation: This is true as stated in Luke 5:12, where a man full of leprosy approached Jesus.

questions.question: True or False: Simon Peter was a tax collector.
questions.explanation: This is true as it is implied that Simon Peter, a fisherman, had a different occupation but was not a tax collector.

questions.question: True or False: The leper asked Jesus to make him rich.
questions.explanation: This is false because the leper asked Jesus to make him clean, not rich, as stated in Luke 5:12.

questions.question: True or False: The disciples caught fish all night long.
questions.explanation: This is false; Simon said they toiled all the night and caught nothing, as stated in Luke 5:5.

medium.title: Luke Chapter 5 Quiz - Medium Level
medium.description: Ready for more? Apply biblical truths from Luke Chapter 5 to real-life situations.

questions.question: What did Jesus tell the man with leprosy to do after healing him?
questions.explanation: Jesus charged him to tell no man but to go and show himself to the priest and offer for his cleansing, as commanded by Moses, for a testimony unto them. (Luke 5:14)

questions.question: What does Luke 5:15 promise will happen if someone seeks to hear and be healed by Jesus?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:15 indicates that because of Jesus' fame, great multitudes came together to hear him and to be healed of their infirmities.

questions.question: What did Jesus do in Luke 5:16?
options: He withdrew into the wilderness and prayed
questions.correctAnswer: He withdrew into the wilderness and prayed
questions.explanation: Luke 5:16 states that Jesus withdrew himself into the wilderness and prayed, indicating his need for solitude and communication with God.

questions.question: In which setting did Jesus teach as described in Luke 5:17?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:17 mentions that Jesus was teaching and Pharisees were present, indicating a more private setting, likely in a house.

questions.question: What did the men do to bring the paralyzed man to Jesus according to Luke 5:19?
options: They carried him on their backs
They found a way through the crowd
They let him down through the tiling
They called for Jesus to come outside
questions.correctAnswer: They let him down through the tiling
questions.explanation: Luke 5:19 describes how, unable to find a way through the multitude, they went upon the housetop and let him down through the tiling with his couch.

questions.question: What did Jesus say to the paralyzed man when he saw their faith in Luke 5:20?
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:20, Jesus saw their faith and said to the sick of the palsy, 'Man, thy sins are forgiven thee.' This demonstrates the connection between faith and forgiveness.

questions.question: What was the reaction of the scribes and Pharisees to Jesus forgiving sins in Luke 5:21?
options: They reasoned that it was blasphemy
They asked him to teach more
questions.correctAnswer: They reasoned that it was blasphemy
questions.explanation: Luke 5:21 indicates that the scribes and Pharisees began to reason among themselves, questioning who Jesus was to forgive sins, which they considered blasphemy.

questions.question: What does Jesus ask the scribes and Pharisees in Luke 5:22?
options: What reason do you have in your hearts?
Who do you say I am?
questions.correctAnswer: What reason do you have in your hearts?
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:22, Jesus perceived their thoughts and asked them, 'What reason ye in your hearts?' challenging their skepticism and understanding.

questions.question: According to Jesus in Luke 5:23, what is easier to say?
questions.explanation: Jesus posed the question in Luke 5:23 to illustrate the challenge of forgiving sins, which is not visible like healing the sick.

questions.question: What did Jesus demonstrate by healing the paralyzed man in Luke 5:24?
options: He had power to forgive sins
He was the Son of God
questions.correctAnswer: He had power to forgive sins
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:24, Jesus declared his authority to forgive sins and demonstrated it by healing the man, signifying his divine power.

questions.question: What was the immediate reaction of the paralyzed man after being healed in Luke 5:25?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:25 states that the man immediately rose up, took his couch, and departed to his house glorifying God, showing his gratitude.

questions.question: How did the people respond to the miracle in Luke 5:26?
options: They were amazed and glorified God
questions.correctAnswer: They were amazed and glorified God
questions.explanation: According to Luke 5:26, the people were all amazed, glorifying God and filled with fear, recognizing the extraordinary nature of what they witnessed.

questions.question: True or False: Jesus instructed the cleansed leper to publicly testify about his healing.
questions.explanation: Jesus instructed the leper to tell no man, as stated in Luke 5:14.

questions.question: True or False: The power of the Lord was present to heal the Pharisees and doctors of the law.
questions.explanation: Luke 5:17 mentions that the power of the Lord was present to heal them, referring to those present including the Pharisees and doctors.

questions.question: True or False: The sick of the palsy was lowered through the roof by his friends to be healed by Jesus.
questions.explanation: While the sick of the palsy was indeed lowered through the roof, the primary purpose was to have his sins forgiven, as stated in Luke 5:20.

hard.title: Luke Chapter 5 Quiz - Hard Level
hard.description: Challenge yourself with deep analysis and cross-biblical connections from Luke Chapter 5.

questions.question: Who did Jesus see sitting at the receipt of custom, whom He then called to follow Him?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:27 states Jesus saw a publican named Levi sitting at the receipt of custom and called him to follow Him.

questions.question: What was Levi's response after Jesus called him?
options: He left all, rose up, and followed Him
He asked for more time to decide
He invited Jesus to his house first
questions.correctAnswer: He left all, rose up, and followed Him
questions.explanation: Luke 5:28 records that Levi left all, rose up, and followed Jesus immediately.

questions.question: What event did Levi organize after following Jesus?
options: A great feast in his house
questions.correctAnswer: A great feast in his house
questions.explanation: Luke 5:29 notes that Levi made a great feast in his own house to celebrate Jesus following him.

questions.question: Who murmured against Jesus’ disciples for eating and drinking with publicans and sinners?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:30 states that the scribes and Pharisees murmured against Jesus’ disciples for associating with publicans and sinners.

questions.question: Jesus said, 'They that are whole need not a physician; but they that are sick.' What is the theological implication of this statement?
options: He came to call sinners to repentance
He only ministers to the righteous
questions.correctAnswer: He came to call sinners to repentance
questions.explanation: Luke 5:31-32 clarify that Jesus came not to call the righteous but sinners to repentance, analogous to a physician healing the sick.

questions.question: In Luke 5, Jesus uses the analogy of new wine and old bottles. What does this parable emphasize?
options: The incompatibility of new teachings with old traditions
questions.correctAnswer: The incompatibility of new teachings with old traditions
questions.explanation: Luke 5:36-38 uses the parable of new wine and old bottles to illustrate that new teachings (new wine) require new frameworks (new bottles), signifying the incompatibility of the new covenant with old Jewish legalism.

questions.question: What does the Greek word 'murmured' (Luke 5:30) mean?
questions.explanation: The Greek word used in Luke 5:30 for 'murmured' (ἐψιθύρισαν) means to grumble or complain secretly or under one's breath.

questions.question: Which literary device is predominantly used in Luke 5:36-39 with the new garment and new wine illustrations?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:36-39 uses parables—short, illustrative stories—to convey spiritual truths about the incompatibility of new teachings with old structures.

questions.question: Which Old Testament passage echoes the theme of calling sinners to repentance found in Luke 5:32?
questions.explanation: Isaiah 1:18 invites sinners to reason together and repent, which echoes Jesus’ call to sinners to repentance in Luke 5:32.

questions.question: Which New Testament passage fulfills the theme of Jesus calling Levi to follow Him as seen in Luke 5:27-28?
questions.explanation: Matthew 9:9 recounts the calling of Matthew (Levi), paralleling Luke 5:27-28 where Jesus calls Levi to follow Him.

questions.question: What event immediately precedes Jesus calling Levi in Luke 5?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:18-26 describes the healing of a man with palsy immediately before Jesus calls Levi in Luke 5:27.

questions.question: How does Luke 5:31-32 exemplify typology in Jesus' ministry?
options: Jesus as the physician typifying the Messiah who heals spiritual sickness
Jesus as a fisherman typifying the gathering of Israel
Jesus as a rabbi typifying Jewish law
Jesus as a king typifying Davidic rule
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus as the physician typifying the Messiah who heals spiritual sickness
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:31-32, Jesus calling sinners to repentance like a physician healing the sick is a typology illustrating His messianic role as healer of spiritual ailments.

questions.question: In the cultural context of Luke 5, why was it controversial for Jesus and His disciples to eat with publicans and sinners?
options: Publicans were seen as unclean and traitors collaborating with Romans
questions.correctAnswer: Publicans were seen as unclean and traitors collaborating with Romans
questions.explanation: Publicans were Jewish tax collectors seen as sinners and traitors collaborating with Romans, making meals with them socially and religiously controversial (Luke 5:30).

questions.question: True or False: According to Luke 5:34-35, Jesus stated that the disciples should fast frequently while the bridegroom is with them.
questions.explanation: Luke 5:34-35 records Jesus saying the children of the bridechamber cannot fast while the bridegroom is with them, but will fast when he is taken away.

questions.question: True or False: Luke 5:39 indicates that people who have experienced the old way immediately desire the new way, saying 'The new is better.'
questions.explanation: Luke 5:39 states no one having drunk old wine immediately desires new wine, because they say 'The old is better,' showing resistance to change.

theological.title: Luke Chapter 5 Quiz - Theological Level
theological.description: Deep biblical theology from Luke Chapter 5 that unites all believers. Explore foundational truths about God, creation, and humanity.

questions.question: What doctrine does Luke 5:5 teach about human response to divine authority in salvation?
options: Human obedience to God's word despite prior failure
Salvation is earned by human labor
Faith is irrelevant to divine intervention
questions.correctAnswer: Human obedience to God's word despite prior failure
questions.explanation: Luke 5:5 shows Simon Peter's willingness to obey Jesus' command to let down the nets despite having caught nothing all night, illustrating that human obedience to divine authority is crucial even when circumstances seem hopeless.

questions.question: What doctrine about Jesus' authority over sin is taught in Luke 5:20?
options: Jesus has authority to forgive sins on earth
Only God the Father can forgive sins
Sin cannot be forgiven in this life
Forgiveness is granted through human intermediaries
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus has authority to forgive sins on earth
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:20, Jesus declares the man's sins forgiven, which reveals his divine authority to forgive sins, a prerogative traditionally ascribed only to God.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of repentance and calling is conveyed in Luke 5:32?
options: Jesus calls sinners to repentance, not the self-righteous
Only the righteous are called to repentance
Sinners are excluded from Jesus' call
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus calls sinners to repentance, not the self-righteous
questions.explanation: Luke 5:32 explicitly states that Jesus came to call sinners to repentance, emphasizing that the call to salvation is directed toward those aware of their sinfulness rather than those who consider themselves righteous.

questions.question: Which divine attribute does Luke 5:24 specifically demonstrate?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:24 demonstrates Jesus' omnipotence as he commands the paralytic to rise and walk, showing his sovereign power over both sin and physical infirmity.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is highlighted in Luke 5:13 when Jesus heals the man with leprosy?
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:13, Jesus' compassionate act of touching and healing the leper demonstrates God's attribute of mercy towards the suffering and outcast.

questions.question: How does Luke 5:11 prepare for the broader biblical theme of discipleship?
options: By illustrating total renunciation to follow Christ
questions.correctAnswer: By illustrating total renunciation to follow Christ
questions.explanation: Luke 5:11 shows the fishermen leaving all and following Jesus, which sets the pattern for the biblical theme that true discipleship requires total commitment and renunciation of worldly attachments.

questions.question: What redemptive-historical connection does Luke 5:14 illustrate?
options: Fulfillment of Mosaic Law purification rites alongside Jesus' healing
Rejection of the Law of Moses
Introduction of a new priesthood replacing Levitical priests
questions.correctAnswer: Fulfillment of Mosaic Law purification rites alongside Jesus' healing
questions.explanation: Luke 5:14 commands the healed leper to present himself to the priest and offer sacrifices as Moses commanded, showing Jesus' respect for the Law while fulfilling its purpose through divine healing.

questions.question: What combined doctrine do Luke 5:20 and Luke 5:24 teach about Jesus' identity and authority?
options: Jesus possesses divine authority to forgive sins and to heal physically
Jesus is only a prophet without divine power
Jesus cannot forgive sins but can heal physically
Jesus' authority is limited to spiritual matters only
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus possesses divine authority to forgive sins and to heal physically
questions.explanation: Luke 5:20 shows Jesus forgiving sins, and Luke 5:24 shows him healing the paralytic, together affirming his divine authority over both spiritual and physical realms.

questions.question: What doctrine about the nature of the kingdom of God is taught by the synthesis of Luke 5:36 and Luke 5:37?
options: The new covenant in Christ requires new structures, not old forms
The old covenant remains fully intact without change
Salvation is achieved by mixing old and new rituals
The kingdom of God is purely political
questions.correctAnswer: The new covenant in Christ requires new structures, not old forms
questions.explanation: Luke 5:36-37 metaphorically teaches that the new wine of the kingdom cannot be contained in old wineskins, symbolizing that Christ's new covenant demands new forms rather than old religious structures.

questions.question: What theological insight emerges from combining Luke 5:31 and Luke 5:32 regarding Christ's mission?
options: Christ's mission is to bring healing and repentance to sinners
Christ came only for the righteous
Christ's mission excludes those who acknowledge sin
Christ's healing is purely physical without spiritual implications
questions.correctAnswer: Christ's mission is to bring healing and repentance to sinners
questions.explanation: Luke 5:31 states that the sick need a physician, and Luke 5:32 clarifies Jesus came to call sinners to repentance, together emphasizing his mission to heal both body and soul.

questions.question: Skeptics claim Jesus' forgiveness of sins in Luke 5:20 is blasphemous because only God can forgive sins. What does Luke 5:20-24 actually teach?
options: Jesus demonstrates his divine authority by forgiving sins and healing, validating his claim to deity
Jesus was mistaken about his authority to forgive sins
Jesus relies on priests to forgive sins for him
Forgiveness of sins was a metaphor for physical healing only
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus demonstrates his divine authority by forgiving sins and healing, validating his claim to deity
questions.explanation: Luke 5:20-24 shows Jesus forgiving the paralytic's sins and healing him physically to prove his authority on earth to forgive sins, affirming his divine nature against accusations of blasphemy.

questions.question: What doctrine about the role of faith in salvation is taught in Luke 5:20 and Luke 5:19?
options: Faith is essential for Jesus to act in forgiveness and healing
Salvation is independent of human faith
Faith is unnecessary when miracles occur
questions.correctAnswer: Faith is essential for Jesus to act in forgiveness and healing
questions.explanation: Luke 5:19 notes Jesus saw the faith of the men who brought the paralytic, and in verse 20 he forgives the man's sins, showing that faith is the key condition for divine forgiveness and healing.

questions.question: Which divine attribute is especially demonstrated in Luke 5:17 when the power of the Lord is present to heal?
questions.explanation: Luke 5:17 reveals God's sovereign power being present to heal, demonstrating his supreme control over nature and human affairs.

questions.question: What theological significance does the feast Levi made in Luke 5:29 have in the narrative of Jesus' ministry?
options: It symbolizes the inclusion of sinners into the kingdom community
It endorses wealth as a sign of divine favor
questions.correctAnswer: It symbolizes the inclusion of sinners into the kingdom community
questions.explanation: Luke 5:29 shows Levi inviting sinners and publicans to a feast with Jesus, highlighting the gospel's inclusive call to those marginalized by religious society.

questions.question: What combined doctrine about the nature of Jesus’ teaching and mission is taught in Luke 5:3 and Luke 5:4?
options: Jesus teaches with authority and initiates the call to active mission
Jesus rejects fishing as a metaphor
questions.correctAnswer: Jesus teaches with authority and initiates the call to active mission
questions.explanation: In Luke 5:3 Jesus teaches from Simon’s boat, and in 5:4 he commands Simon to launch into deep water and fish, symbolizing the call to discipleship and mission.
